newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin on target for Kremlin return at New Year.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin on target for Kremlin return at New Year.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is in satisfactory condition six days after heart surgery and is on target to return to the Kremlin as planned around the New Year, his chief doctor said on Monday.

Sergei Mironov, head of the presidential medical centre, said the president was quickly becoming more active, his appetite was returning and he was walking and sitting up for six hours a day after his quintuple bypass operation on November 5.

But Mironov added a word of caution, making clear he did not want the 65-year-old president to try to set "world records" by coming back too quickly and that bad news was being served up to him with due care.

"The condition of Boris Nikolayevich is satisfactory," Mironov told a news conference. "Boris Yeltsin's post-operative stitches are healing well, his blood counts are very good and his temperature is normal for the fourth day in a row."

Mironov said Yeltsin would probably spend from 12 to 14 more days in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital and a month in the Barvikha sanatorium just outside Moscow where he spent much of the time when he was preparing for the operation.
He declined to set any dates but said Yeltsin's progress was normal and in line with the timetable foreseen by the surgeons who carried out the operation.
"I think that for the time being we are going according to the existing norms. I think the process of rehabilitation in the clinic and sanatorium will last about 1-1/2 months to two months," he said.
That would put him on target for a return to the Kremlin around the New Year holiday, a major celebration in the Russian calendar.

But playing down the talk of target dates, Mironov said doctors were more interested in Yeltsin's long-term recovery than setting any short-term goals such as whether he would see out his second term as president which expires in the year 2000.
"We want to go a marathon distance of 10, 12, 15 years. Of course you can set a new world record...but we are not setting ourselves such a goal," he said.
"Our basic task, as we said earlier, is restoring the president's real work capacity."

Yeltsin has issued some decrees from hospital and received Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Kremlin chief of staff Anatoly Chubais. He sent a message on Monday condemning a bomb attack on a Moscow cemetery on Sunday which killed 13 people.
In a sign that doctors are still treading carefully, Mironov said Yeltsin was being shielded from some "negative information".
It was not clear what he meant by this because the president was informed about Sunday's bloody bomb attack.
"It is after all only six days and not since weeks (since the operation) and so we try to protect Boris Nikolayevich from any unnecessary wave of negative information," Mironov said.
He said such a procedure was natural and that Yeltsin was still being well informed by his aides.

Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and one of his doctors said he probably had a third just before his re-election on July 3. He has spent only a handful of days in the Kremlin since he was re-elected.
Doctors see Yeltsin every day at the Central Clinical Hospital and meet to discuss his condition.
